JAC

messages.body_plain:
Strange! The parallel stuff works very well in Linux. Could you try the following?

* I see you are running from the R shell. After you get the error above, could you execute "traceback()"  and send me the output?

* Could you try to repeat the same but adding the scenario setting "loadBalancing=FALSE"?

* Could you try to run the following commands in R?

library(parallel)
simplify2array(mclapply(rep(4, 5), rnorm, mc.cores=4))

* After the error, does irace create a file named iracedump or something similar? If so, could you send it to me?

*  After the error, does irace create a file irace.Rdata? If so, could you send it to me?

* Could you also send me the output generated when using parallel=1 instead of parallel=4?

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.subject: Push Formula on Homebrew
messages.body_plain:
I think I would be nice if user can easily install the command line tool from homebrew without interacting with CRAN / R. I drafted a homebrew formula and opened a PR. Please feel free to give any feedback or provide any help.

https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/pull/98816

In particular, I couldn't figure out how to install it in a way that does not require the user to manually set the R_LIBS environment variable. Homebrew would not give me permission to install it in the system level R library (for good reasons).

messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] Push Formula on Homebrew
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for trying anyway. Don't be too worried about it because CRAN provides binaries for MacOS, so it is easy to do 'install.packages("irace")' without requiring anything else besides installing R.

For the development version, it is slightly more complex because you need a C compiler installed, but once you have that, it should be a matter of doing: "devtools::install_github("MLopez-Ibanez/irace")".

R is not great. If I had to start implementing irace today, I would choose Python (or possibly Julia), but reimplementing everything is Python or Julia is beyond my available time now. But I'll be happy if somebody started such a project. If you are planning such a project, get in touch with me, I can offer you some guidance so you can avoid some "mistakes" we did along the way in R's irace.

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.body_plain:
I am currently trying to use iRACE for parameter tuning of a metaheuristic implemented in C++. I have a number of questions and I request to answer to my doubts and queries.

1. I have listed the parameters in "parameters.txt". I don't know how these parameter values will be read by my program?
2. The cost was being written in an output file but I don't know how it will be sent to the target-runner file?
3. Please let me know if the following are to be kept as such in the target-runner file in our implementation as I am unable to understand its significance.
CONFIG_ID="$1"
INSTANCE_ID="$2"
SEED="$3"
INSTANCE=''$4

4. I am attaching the list of commands which I used to run iRACE for tuning of the parameters. I am getting an error (attached below) while running these commands to run my code. Please check.
"

I hope my doubts and queries would be rectified.

Thank you.

and it contains a step-by-step example using a C program (ACOTSP), so very close to what you are trying to do.
All your doubts and queries are answered in the guide already. Please read it in detail, it took us many hours to write it.

Cheers,

Manuel.
